verdict: WTW grew revenue 8% to $2.46B on 4% organic growth plus acquisitions, but $56M of restructuring and deal costs held GAAP profit flat at $309M even as adjusted EPS rose 18%.

segments.name: Health, Wealth & Career
segments.note: Advice and solutions for employee health benefits, retirement and careers — WTW's larger segment, with segment operating income of $398M, a 29% margin.

segments.name: Risk & Broking
segments.note: Insurance broking and risk advice for companies — placing coverage and negotiating with insurers, with segment operating income of $216M, a 20% margin.

segments.name: Corporate and reimbursable items
segments.note: Costs incurred on behalf of clients and reimbursed by them, plus other items WTW does not count in segment revenue — the bridge from segment revenue ($2,437M) to GAAP revenue ($2,460M).

opex.name: Other operating expenses
opex.note: Day-to-day running costs other than people — offices, technology, travel and professional fees.

opex.name: Amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of intangible assets bought in acquisitions over their useful lives.

opex.name: Depreciation
opex.note: Spreading the cost of buildings, equipment and software over their useful lives.

opex.name: Transaction and program expenses
opex.note: Deal and program costs — mainly share-based compensation and transaction costs for the Newfront and Cushon acquisitions, plus Propel AI plan integration.

opex.name: Restructuring costs
opex.note: One-off costs of Propel, WTW's AI Acceleration Plan.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $80M and a $13M loss from interests in associates, partly offset by $52M of other income — a net $41M cost below operating income.
oneTimers: Restructuring costs of $14M for Propel, WTW's AI Acceleration Plan (there were none in this line a year ago).
Transaction and program expenses of $42M, mainly share-based compensation and other transaction-related costs for the Newfront and Cushon acquisitions and Propel integration — up from $2M a year ago.

takeaways.title: Organic growth held up
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 8% as reported, of which 4% was organic — the rest came from acquisitions and currency. Health, Wealth & Career grew 7% and Risk & Broking 8% on a reported basis.

takeaways.title: Adjusted EPS jumped 18%
takeaways.text: Adjusted diluted EPS was $3.63 versus GAAP $3.24, and the adjusted operating margin widened to 21.9% from 20.4% — the deal and restructuring costs are the gap between the two views.

takeaways.title: One-off costs flattened GAAP profit
takeaways.text: Restructuring ($14M) plus transaction and program expenses ($42M) are why net income was nearly flat at $309M versus $306M despite 8% revenue growth; the GAAP operating margin slipped to 17.4% from 18.3%.

footerNote: WTW prints a single 'Costs of providing services' block. This page treats salaries and benefits ($1,507M) — the people who deliver the advice and broking — as the direct cost of revenue, so gross profit is revenue less that people cost; the rest of the printed block sits in operating expenses, and the totals tie exactly to the printed income from operations of $429M. Segment figures are WTW's segment revenue measure; adding $23M of reimbursable expenses and other items reaches GAAP revenue. Net income of $309M is consolidated; $303M was attributable to WTW shareholders after $6M for noncontrolling interests.
